official.deadline_note: The fee-waiver window is open from October to mid-December 2026; the scholarship's own application deadline has not been published on the programme page as of 10 October 2026. Applicants are told to consult the Sciences Po Admissions website for the Master's admissions timeline, and to apply by the earliest applicable deadline if seeking more than one scholarship.
official.status_note: The programme page states that applications for the application fee waiver will be open from October to mid-December 2026, with several information sessions between September and December 2026 and a virtual Open House on 17 October 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholarships cover the full cost of tuition and living expenses in France, throughout the recipient's time studying at Sciences Po. The Program covers the full financial needs of selected Scholars.
benefits: Full financial needs covered for the two years of Master's study at Sciences Po
Application fee waiver as part of the eligibility process
Housing in Paris reserved for Mastercard Foundation Scholars
Careers support, a careers fair focused on employment and internship opportunities in Africa, and access to the entrepreneurship track, the business incubator and the alumni employer network
A mentoring programme co-run with the Africa Division of Sciences Po Alumni
Support from the moment candidates are selected until they secure their first job
eligibility: Hold the citizenship of an African country; applicants holding dual citizenship that includes citizenship of a country outside the African continent are not eligible
Be currently completing, or already hold, a Bachelor's degree from one of the universities on the published list of institutions
Or have participated in a recognised bridge programme or mentoring programme offered by one of the approved organisations
Or currently hold, or have previously held, UNHCR refugee status
Be under 35 years of age on 1 September of the year in which the scholarship application is submitted
Not already hold, or currently be pursuing, a Master's degree
Be applying to the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for the first time
Meet Sciences Po's minimum academic result requirement for the country of the home university
Be applying to a two-year Master's programme at Sciences Po through the International Graduate Admissions Procedure; dual degree programmes and one-year Master's programmes are not eligible
Students currently enrolled at Sciences Po, or currently enrolled in or graduated from, a French higher education institution are not eligible
requirements: Demonstrate a clear alignment between the chosen Master's programme, personal and academic background and future career goals
Demonstrate critical thinking and analytical insight into the major contemporary political, economic and societal challenges facing Africa and the world
Demonstrate ambition, originality and perseverance through entrepreneurial initiatives or public service projects with potential to contribute to Africa's socio-economic transformation
Submit a complete application; any missing or non-compliant supporting document renders the application incomplete and therefore ineligible
Consult the mandatory table of minimum academic results before applying; applicants who do not meet this threshold are automatically deemed ineligible
documents: A valid identity document (passport, national identity card, or travel document)
Proof of a completed or in-progress Bachelor's degree (transcript, diploma or certificate) from a recognised partner university
Or proof of a completed or in-progress Bachelor's degree plus a certificate confirming successful completion of a recognised bridge programme
Or proof of a completed or in-progress Bachelor's degree plus proof of refugee status (UNHCR registration card)
Language test results as required by the chosen Master's programme
Letters of recommendation, which must not be submitted from a personal email address
selection_criteria: Having faced significant barriers to accessing education, whether economic, social, geographical or resulting from other circumstances

Demonstrating a strong commitment to advancing the development of the African continent and a clear aspiration to become a changemaker, particularly in public policy and political, environmental and societal transitions
Demonstrating strong potential for transformative leadership, together with the capacity and determination to create a positive, sustainable and measurable impact
Particular consideration is given to applications from young women, refugees and displaced persons, and persons with disabilities
coverage: The full financial needs of selected Scholars for the two years of study at Sciences Po
Full cost of tuition in France
The page does not publish any travel, flight or installation allowance
application_method: Check eligibility against the published criteria and the table of minimum academic results
Apply for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program and request an application fee waiver through the Sciences Po application platform during the October to mid-December 2026 window
If the eligibility criteria are met, receive a message explaining the steps to complete and submit the application with the fee waived
Apply to and be admitted to a two-year Master's programme through the International Graduate Admissions Procedure
If shortlisted, attend an online interview conducted via Zoom
official.application_route: Request the application fee waiver on the Sciences Po application platform, then apply for admission to a two-year Master's via the International Graduate Admissions Procedure and await Selection Committee review.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must hold the citizenship of an African country; dual citizenship including a country outside the African continent is excluded. Students currently enrolled in, or graduated from, a French higher education institution are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Open to citizens of African countries only, including applicants holding or having held UNHCR refugee status.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The Bachelor's degree must come from a listed partner institution, or from a recognised bridge or mentoring programme offered by an approved organisation, or the applicant must hold or have held UNHCR refugee status. The Master's programme must be a two-year Sciences Po programme; dual degree and one-year Master's programmes are not eligible.
official.duration: Two years of Master's study at Sciences Po
official.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po is the first such programme in continental Europe and is designed for students from the African continent who wish to pursue a two-year Master's degree at Sciences Po. The Program covers the full financial needs of selected Scholars and provides comprehensive support throughout their two years of study, from selection through to first employment.
official.english_requirement: Language test results as required by the chosen Master's programme; no single minimum score is published on the scholarship page.

applicant_utility.summary: The first gate is not the scholarship at all - it is the application fee waiver, and it only opens between October and mid-December 2026, so the practical deadline to watch is the waiver window rather than a scholarship closing date. Two hard exclusions catch strong candidates every year: holding any Master's already or being enrolled in one, and having studied at a French higher education institution. Your Bachelor's degree must come from the published partner-institution list, or from an approved bridge or mentoring programme, or you must hold or have held UNHCR refugee status - if it comes from nowhere on those lists, this route closes regardless of your record.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Under-35 African citizens, ideally with a degree from a listed partner institution or an approved bridge programme, who can evidence concrete public-service or entrepreneurial action and want a fully funded two-year Master's in Paris.
application_readiness_checklist: Search the published partner-institution PDF for your exact university, and the bridge-programme list if you used one, before investing time in the application
Open the country-by-country table of minimum academic results and check your transcript against your own country's row - below the threshold is an automatic rejection, not a discretionary one
Request the fee waiver in the October to mid-December 2026 window and keep the confirmation message with your application steps
Brief referees early that recommendations sent from a personal email address will make the file non-compliant, and give them institutional addresses
Draft the written assignments around your own documented projects - the page warns that use of AI may result in a lower evaluation
Diarise the 17 October 2026 virtual Open House and any autumn admissions webinars, since they are the only scheduled touchpoints published
common_rejection_risks: A missing or non-compliant attachment - transcripts, language test results or a recommendation from a personal email address all make the file incomplete and therefore ineligible
Falling below the mandatory minimum academic result for your home university's country, which is applied automatically before any merit review
Applying to a one-year Master's or a dual degree programme, both of which are excluded from consideration
Being currently enrolled at Sciences Po, or enrolled in or graduated from any French higher education institution
Applying for the Programme after having already applied once - it must be your first application
Turning 35 before 1 September of the application year, or holding dual citizenship that includes a non-African country
Deferring a Sciences Po admission by a year, which voids the scholarship offer entirely
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not published. The award is described as covering full financial needs, tuition and living expenses for two years, but no figure is given and no travel allowance is mentioned, so applicants should assume any flight, visa, insurance or pre-departure cost is on them until the offer letter states otherwise.
document_audit: The identity document must be valid at the time of the waiver request - an expired passport is a common and avoidable failure
If your Bachelor's is still in progress, the transcript must show it clearly as in-progress rather than complete
Refugee-status claims need the UNHCR registration card itself, not a letter from a third party
Bridge-programme claims need two items: the Bachelor's proof and the completion certificate for the recognised programme
Recommendations must arrive from institutional email addresses; confirm this with referees before they submit
alerts: Several months may elapse between a Sciences Po admission offer and the scholarship decision, so do not decline other funding while waiting
An offer to join the Programme is valid only for the academic year for which it is issued - deferring by one year makes you ineligible
Meeting eligibility criteria and being admitted to Sciences Po does not guarantee an interview, and an interview invitation does not guarantee the award
If you are admitted but not selected, you are responsible for securing alternative funding - there is no partial fallback described
The page states that detailed information and the application timeline will be published shortly, so re-read it during the October to mid-December 2026 window
If you intend to apply for more than one scholarship, submit by the earliest applicable deadline
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Fee-waiver request on the Sciences Po platform, then admission application to a two-year Master's through the International Graduate Admissions Procedure, then Selection Committee review with a roughly 25-minute Zoom interview for shortlisted admitted candidates.
